question: Who should you use standard precautions for in the ward?

options.A: All patients receiving care regardless of diagnosis
options.B: Visitors and administrative staff members only
options.C: Patients admitted specifically to isolation wards
options.D: Only patients with confirmed infectious diseases

explanation: Great job! Standard precautions are meant for EVERY patient, every single time. Since we don't always know who might be carrying an infection, treating everyone with these safety rules keeps both you and your patients safe.

question: How do standard precautions mainly stop infections from spreading?

options.A: By destroying the infectious agent inside the human body
options.B: By completely eliminating the natural reservoir of pathogens
options.C: By increasing the natural immunity of the susceptible host
options.D: By blocking the mode of transmission and portal of entry

explanation: You got it! Think of gloves and masks as road blockers. They stop germs from traveling from the patient to you, breaking the chain of infection right in the middle.

question: When MUST you use soap and water instead of an alcohol hand rub?

options.A: Immediately after removing clean, non-sterile examination gloves
options.B: Before taking a patient's routine blood pressure reading
options.C: When entering a patient room for a brief verbal assessment
options.D: When hands are visibly soiled with dirt or body fluids

explanation: Spot on! If your hands have visible dirt, blood, or body fluids on them, alcohol rubs just won't cut it. You need good old soap and water to physically wash the mess away.

question: You just finished taking a patient's temperature and pulse. What is your next move?

options.A: Perform hand hygiene immediately after touching the patient
options.B: Wipe hands with a dry paper towel without using soap
options.C: Wash hands only if the patient reports feeling unwell
options.D: Sanitize hands only before entering the next patient's room

explanation: Well done! Always clean your hands right after touching a patient. It's the easiest way to make sure you don't carry their germs to the next bed.

question: What is the very first thing you put on when wearing a full set of PPE?
explanation: That's correct! Always start with your gown, tying it securely to cover your uniform first. Your gloves always go on last, right over the gown sleeves.

question: Why do we take off our gloves FIRST before removing other PPE items?

options.A: Gloves are usually the most contaminated items touched during care
options.B: Gloves are the only reusable item in the standard PPE set
options.C: Gloves interfere with untying the back of the protective gown
options.D: Gloves take the longest time to take off safely

explanation: Exactly! Your gloves have touched all the germs, so taking them off first stops you from accidentally smearing those pathogens onto your face or mask while undressing.

question: What is the golden rule for using syringes and needles in patient care?

options.A: They can be shared between family members in the same room
options.B: They are single-use devices and must never be reused
options.C: They can be reused if sterilized in boiling water first
options.D: They only need replacement if they appear bent or blunt

explanation: Spot on! Needles and syringes are strictly single-use. Reusing them is a fast track to spreading deadly bloodborne infections like HIV and Hepatitis.

question: Why shouldn't you fill a sharps container past its fill line?

options.A: It prevents the hospital from recycling the plastic material
options.B: It makes the container too heavy for the waste collectors
options.C: It increases the risk of accidental needle-stick injuries
options.D: It causes the plastic walls of the container to melt

explanation: You got it! Overfilling sharps bins means needles start poking out or pushing against the lid, putting anyone handling the bin at high risk of a needle-stick injury.

question: If you don't have a tissue handy and suddenly need to cough, what should you do?

options.B: Cough directly into the open air
options.C: Turn your head toward the nearest wall
options.D: Cover your mouth with both bare hands

explanation: Brilliant! Coughing into your elbow keeps the droplets off your hands. If you cough into your hands, you'll just transfer those germs to every door handle and chart you touch!

question: When should respiratory hygiene measures start for a patient visiting the hospital?

options.A: At the very first point of entry into the facility
options.B: Only when the patient requests a protective face mask
options.C: After the patient is admitted to an inpatient ward
options.D: Only after a doctor confirms a respiratory diagnosis

explanation: That's right! Catching coughs and handing out masks right at the reception or triage desk stops airborne bugs from spreading in a crowded waiting room.

question: Which of these waste items goes into a rigid, puncture-resistant container?

options.A: Soiled paper hand towels and napkins
options.D: Clean cotton balls and packaging paper

explanation: Correct! Sharp items like blades and needles need hard, puncture-proof walls so they don't poke through and injure nurses or waste handlers.

question: Why must you follow the manufacturer's recommended contact time for a disinfectant?

options.A: It allows the surface to dry completely without wiping
options.B: It reduces the financial cost of purchasing cleaning supplies
options.C: It ensures the chemical agent has enough time to kill pathogens
options.D: It prevents the disinfectant liquid from staining hospital furniture

explanation: You got it! Disinfectants aren't magic—they need a few minutes of wet contact time to actually break down and destroy stubborn germs on a surface.

question: What is the very first thing you should do after an accidental needle-stick injury?

options.A: Cover the bleeding wound tightly with a waterproof bandage
options.B: Squeeze the puncture site firmly to force out old blood
options.C: Wash the affected area thoroughly with soap and water
options.D: Apply a strong antiseptic alcohol solution to seal the cut

explanation: Spot on! Don't panic. Calmly wash the area right away with plenty of soap and running water to flush out as many germs as possible.

question: Why should you avoid squeezing or scrubbing a needle-stick injury site?

options.A: It can cause local tissue trauma and drive pathogens deeper
options.B: It increases the immediate bleeding time and delays healing
options.C: It prevents the wound from forming a natural scab layer
options.D: It neutralizes the effectiveness of subsequent soap washing

explanation: Well done! Squeezing or scrubbing might feel like a good idea, but it actually damages your tissues and can push the infectious material deeper into your bloodstream.
